AUTHOR: Engel
TITLE: Space partitioning within groups of social coral reef fish
REGION: Eilat fringing reef, northern Gulf of Aqaba, Red Sea, Israel
DATA: Own in situ 3-GoPro stereo/3D video of 4 tagged groups, 15 runs (2015, 2017)
V_EV: Methods (Study species): groups 'found at 9–14 m depth'; model trained 'to detect D. marginatus in the wild under changing lightning and background'
D2: not reported (training details deferred to Engel et al. 2021)
D_EV: no statement found (only 'Using transfer learning, we trained the model to detect D. marginatus'; split not described)
R_EV: Study site: single reef 'in front of the Interuniversity Institute for Marine Sciences in Eilat'; no external evaluation
C_EV: Methods: 'Ambiguities such as occlusions or fish entering and exiting the branching coral were resolved manually using a custom code'
E_EV: Results: 'individual fish maintained foraging spaces that were well separated'; 'mean (± SD) percentage of overlap of foraging spaces was 1.4 (± 3)%'
ARCH: Faster R-CNN Inception V2 detection + frame linking, DLT 3D reconstruction
METR: detection rate (% of time detected) per run; ecological metrics (foraging volume, overlap, shading)
NOTE: Ecology application paper; detector validation published separately (Engel et al. 2021). Only quantitative AI output reported here is per-run detection rate (Table 1, 6-100%), so INCL criterion (c) borderline. No detection accuracy metrics, no comparison to independent reference. Tracking ID ambiguities corrected manually (coded C5). Data on figshare.
